screening_results.reason: Meets inclusion criteria: I1 (English-language empirical article in NeuroImage with original data), I2 (fMRI conducted while humans performed risky and ambiguous decision-making tasks), and I3 (human adolescent sample). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET or review) are met based on the abstract. Include for full-text review to extract coordinates and task details.

Abstract reports an English-language empirical fMRI study in human participants performing risky and ambiguous decision-making tasks; meets I1, I2, and I3. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET-only or review) are met. Include for full-text review.

Human fMRI study of decision-making with original empirical data addressing ambiguity in intertemporal choices (time-ambiguity). Fits review topic (ambiguous decision-making) and all inclusion criteria appear met; no exclusion criteria met from abstract.

Abstract reports original English-language empirical fMRI study of decision-making under risk and ambiguity in humans (patients with schizophrenia and healthy controls). All inclusion criteria are met; no exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract. Recommend full-text review for meta-analysis inclusion.

Abstract describes an English-language empirical study using functional MRI in human participants investigating second-order uncertainty/ambiguity in decision-making, matching the review focus. No exclusion criteria (non-fMRI or review) are met.

The abstract reports an fMRI study in humans examining neural responses to ambiguity and risk. However, participants underwent passive outcome prediction (no explicit decisions), so it is unclear whether this meets the meta-analysis’ decision-making task requirement. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to confirm whether the paradigm qualifies as a decision-making task.

Meets inclusion: original empirical fMRI study in humans performing a probabilistic (risky) decision-making task; participants are adolescent girls (human sample). No exclusion criteria met (not PET/review). Abstract provides sufficient detail to include for full-text review.

Empirical fMRI study in humans performing risky (probabilistic) and intertemporal decision tasks; reports original data and neural activation during decisions. Risky choice falls within the review objective. No exclusion criteria met (not PET/review).

Fits inclusion criteria: English empirical study with original data (I1); fMRI conducted during risky decision-making tasks (ART and BART) (I2); sample of healthy adult humans (I3). No exclusion criteria met (not PET-only, not a review). Include for full-text review.

English-language empirical study using fMRI while human adolescents and young adults performed risky and ambiguous decision-making tasks; meets I1, I2, and I3. No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review.

Abstract reports an original English-language fMRI study of decision-making under risk and ambiguity in human pathological gamblers and controls; meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

Title indicates original empirical study of neural mechanisms and risky decision-making in adolescent cannabis use disorder, but abstract does not explicitly state fMRI was used or that a decision-making task was administered. Inclusion uncertain for I2; include for full-text review to confirm fMRI and task details.

English-language empirical fMRI study in human adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune). All inclusion criteria met and no exclusion criteria apply; include for full-text review.

Abstract reports original empirical fMRI data (English) using a two-choice probabilistic monetary ‘wheel of fortune’ decision-making task in healthy adult humans, meeting I1, I2, and I3. No exclusion criteria (e.g., non-fMRI or review) are met. Recommend full-text review for data extraction.

Abstract reports an original English-language fMRI study where human participants performed an adapted Iowa Gambling Task (risky decision-making). Participants include clinical and healthy groups; no exclusion criteria (e.g., PET or review) are met.
Empirical fMRI study in humans using the Iowa Gambling Task, an ambiguous decision-making task; original data and analyses reported. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports an English-language empirical fMRI study with original data measuring BOLD during perceptual decision-making tasks in human participants (behavioral performance reported). No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria I1 (English-language empirical study) and I3 (human healthy participants) are satisfied. English-language empirical fMRI study reporting original data on human (elderly healthy) participants performing a decision-making task with explicit probabilities (risky decision-making). Abstract indicates fMRI BOLD measured during task and no exclusion criteria (e.g., PET-only or review) are met. Include for full-text review.

Original empirical fMRI study in English applying a probabilistic decision-making task (fits risky/ambiguous decision-making) in human participants (schizophrenia patients and healthy controls). No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract. Recommend inclusion for full-text review.

Meets inclusion criteria: English empirical study with original data (I1); whole-brain fMRI conducted while humans performed a risky/sequential gambling decision-making task (I2); sample comprised healthy human participants (I3). No exclusion criteria met (not PET or review).

Abstract reports an empirical fMRI study (English) of probabilistic decision-making in human participants in an at-risk mental state (a neuropsychiatric group). Empirical fMRI study in humans performing a value-based decision-making task examining unexpected uncertainty, risk, and estimation uncertainty. This meets I1 (English original empirical data), I2 (fMRI during a decision-making task), and I3 (human participants). No exclusion criteria are met from abstract information.

Abstract reports an English-language empirical fMRI study in humans examining choices between certain outcomes and risky gambles, meeting inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I3. No exclusion criteria (e.g., non-fMRI or review) are met. Include for full-text review to confirm details.

Abstract reports an original empirical fMRI study in humans examining decision-making under ambiguity and sample-space ignorance, directly relevant to the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I3 are met. No exclusion criteria (E1, E2) apply.

Abstract reports an English-language empirical fMRI study with original data in humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (emotional face categorization). All inclusion criteria (I1, I2, I3) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met. Recommend full-text review.

Abstract reports an English-language empirical fMRI study in humans performing a dynamic perceptual decision-making task, meeting inclusion criteria for original data, fMRI during task, and human sample. No exclusion criteria are met based on abstract.

Abstract describes an English-language empirical fMRI study with original data (I1), conducted during a risky decision-making task (Risky-Gains) using fMRI (I2), and reports results from healthy human participants (I3). No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract. Include for full-text review.

fMRI study with original human data examining probabilistic (risky) and intertemporal decision making; meets inclusion criteria I1 (English empirical original data), I2 (fMRI during risky decision-making), and I3 (human volunteer sample). No exclusion criteria (non-fMRI or review) apply. Recommend full-text inclusion for meta-analysis screening.

Abstract reports an empirical experiment on the neurobiological influence of expert advice on financial decisions under risk but does not explicitly state that fMRI was used or detail the participant sample. Include for full-text review to confirm fMRI and participant details.

fMRI empirical study with original data on human decision-making under ambiguity/conflict matching meta-analysis scope; participants appear to be human (likely healthy). Provides neural and behavioral data relevant to risky/ambiguous decision-making.
Human fMRI single-case empirical study assessing decision-making under risk and ambiguity with pre- and postsurgical fMRI; meets language, task, and sample criteria. No exclusion criteria met.

Empirical fMRI study in humans performing a risky decision-making task (choices between high- and low-risk rewards); computational modeling of trial-by-trial expected value and prediction error. Meets I1 (original empirical data), I2 (fMRI during risky decision-making), and I3 (human sample). No exclusion criteria (not PET-only or a review) are met.
Abstract reports original human fMRI data during a risky decision-making (mixed gambles) task, in English, with participant sample appropriate for inclusion. No exclusion criteria met.

Original empirical fMRI study in humans examining risky and ambiguous decision-making, matching the review focus. Abstract indicates fMRI during decision tasks and human participants (likely healthy), satisfying I1–I3. No exclusion criteria (no PET/review) are met.

The abstract reports an English-language empirical fMRI study (3T) in human participants who performed the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (a risky decision-making task). It meets I1, I2, and I3, and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical study reporting original data in English, using fMRI to examine neural tracking of subjective value during risky and ambiguous decision-making in a human adolescent sample (N=188), thus meeting I1, I2, and I3. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports original empirical human data (20 IGD, 16 HCs) collected with fMRI during risk-taking and risky decision-making tasks, meeting inclusion criteria I1-I3. Meets I1: English-language empirical study with original data; I2: fMRI was conducted during a decision-making task involving uncertainty/risk (aviation go-around task with stimulus ambiguity); I3: human participants. Abstract reports original empirical fMRI data in humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (Mooney face detection). Include for full-text review to confirm participant eligibility and extract coordinates/results.

English-language empirical fMRI study collecting original data during a probabilistic reversal learning (decision-making) task in healthy human adolescents and adults, meeting inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I3; no exclusion criteria met.

Event-related fMRI study in English reporting original data on risk-taking decisions in human participants (high- vs low-risk choices). Satisfies I1 and I2. Meets all inclusion criteria: English empirical study with original data; used fMRI during a risky decision-making task in human healthy participants. No exclusion criteria met (not PET or review). Recommend inclusion for full-text review.

The abstract reports original empirical fMRI experiments in humans using decision-making tasks (Iowa Gambling Task — ambiguous/unknown probability — and a probability-known risk decision task) addressing prediction updating; this meets I1, I2, and I3. Abstract describes an English-language empirical fMRI study with original data in human adolescents performing risky decision-making tasks in the scanner (before/after social exclusion). Abstract reports an original, English-language fMRI study in humans performing a perceptual decision task (RDM) combined with lottery choices—meets I1, I2, and I3. No exclusion criteria (non-fMRI or review) apply.
fMRI study in humans performing a probabilistic (risky/uncertain) decision-making task with original empirical data; meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

Meets inclusion criteria: English original empirical study (I1) that used fMRI during a simulated driving task involving risky decision-making (I2) with human adolescent participants (I3). No exclusion criteria (non-fMRI or review) apply from the abstract.

English-language empirical fMRI study with original data in healthy young adults. Empirical human fMRI study (lottery choice task) on risky decision-making in older adults, meeting inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I3; no exclusion criteria met and abstract provides sufficient info to include for full-text review.

Empirical fMRI study in humans performing a risky economic decision-making task; meets I1 (original English empirical data), I2 (fMRI during risky decision-making task), and I3 (human sample). No exclusion criteria are met. Recommend inclusion for full-text review.

English-language empirical study with original data; used fMRI while participants performed the Risky Gains Task (risky decision-making); sample: human adults including clinical group (obesity) and healthy controls. No exclusion criteria met (not PET/review).
